steps.intent: The United States aims to secure a unified Council condemnation of the DPRK’s 25 May ICBM launch, reaffirm existing sanctions, and keep pressure on Pyongyang while offering a humanitarian and diplomatic off-ramp. The main difficulty is avoiding a Russian or Chinese veto: this draft therefore focuses on reaffirming existing measures and does not impose new sanctions, but even strong condemnation and the threat of further measures may lead to abstentions or a veto. Negotiations will likely center on the language in paragraphs 1 and 4 and on humanitarian exemptions.

messages.Albania: Albania supports the draft in its current form. We welcome its clear condemnation of the 25 May ICBM launch and its demand that the DPRK cease all ballistic missile launches and abandon its nuclear programmes. We urge the Council to speak with one voice and ensure full implementation of existing sanctions, while preserving humanitarian exemptions for the civilian population.
messages.Brazil: Brazil supports the core of the draft and its clear condemnation of the 25 May ICBM launch. We ask that OP4 be framed as consideration of further measures in accordance with the Charter rather than an open-ended readiness for significant measures, and that OP7 call on all parties to pursue a peaceful, diplomatic and political solution and refrain from escalating tensions. We also ask that OP6 request the 1718 Committee to process humanitarian exemption requests fully, promptly and transparently, including for COVID-19 assistance.
messages.China: China supports the Council’s role in promoting denuclearization and peace and stability on the Korean Peninsula, but the current draft is unbalanced and escalatory. We cannot accept OP4’s threat of further significant measures; this is a red line. We also seek a balanced OP1, stronger calls for dialogue and de-escalation, and effective humanitarian exemptions, together with language on the Panel’s confidentiality.
messages.France: France supports the draft’s strong condemnation of the 25 May ICBM launch and its reaffirmation of the DPRK’s CVID obligations. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP3 with additional sanctions measures, in line with the Council’s prior commitments, particularly on refined petroleum and tobacco. We also want OP4 to commit the Council to further targeted measures without delay and OP5 to cover sanctions evasion, including cyber and financial networks. Humanitarian exemptions must remain full and expedited.
messages.Gabon: Gabon supports the thrust of the draft and its clear condemnation of the 25 May ICBM launch. We ask the penholder to make clear that any further measures will be considered by the Council rather than treated as automatic, to broaden the dialogue appeal to all relevant parties, and to strengthen language on unimpeded humanitarian access and COVID-19 vaccines. We are ready to support a balanced text that preserves Council unity and prioritizes diplomacy.
messages.Ghana: Ghana supports the draft’s clear condemnation of the 25 May ICBM launch and its reaffirmation of the sanctions regime. We ask the penholder to adjust OP4 to preserve Council deliberation on any further measures and to strengthen OP6, OP7 and OP8 so that humanitarian exemptions, COVID-19 assistance, restraint and dialogue are unmistakable. With those changes, Ghana is ready to support the text.
messages.India: India supports the draft’s condemnation of the 25 May ICBM launch and its reaffirmation of existing Council measures. We would ask the penholder to make OP5 explicit on Panel incident reports, as India requested in March, and to broaden OP7 to emphasize dialogue and diplomacy by all relevant parties. With those changes, India is ready to support the text.
messages.Ireland: Ireland strongly supports a clear, unified Council response to the DPRK’s 25 May ICBM launch and welcomes the draft’s condemnation. We ask that OP4 cover all ballistic missile launches and other destabilizing actions, not only ICBMs or nuclear tests, and that the humanitarian paragraphs be strengthened to guarantee timely exemptions and safe, unimpeded access for humanitarian and COVID-19 assistance, including for women, girls and vulnerable groups. We would also welcome a preambular reference to the human rights situation in the DPRK. Ireland remains ready to engage constructively to secure the broadest possible support.
messages.Kenya: Kenya supports the Council’s clear condemnation of the 25 May ICBM launch and the reaffirmation of existing sanctions. We ask that the text strengthen practical humanitarian exemptions and Committee guidance, and that it call on the DPRK to facilitate unimpeded humanitarian delivery, especially for COVID-19 assistance. Kenya would also like a call on all parties to exercise restraint and create conditions for diplomacy. We can support the draft with these changes.
messages.Mexico: Mexico supports the draft’s condemnation of the DPRK’s ballistic missile launches and its reaffirmation of the sanctions regime, and we welcome the humanitarian provisions. We ask that OP5 be strengthened to explicitly mandate the Panel of Experts to investigate and report expeditiously on ballistic missile launch incidents, including the type of missiles, technology and capacities involved, as Mexico sought in March. We also propose adding a preambular reference to the IAEA’s reports on the apparent restart of the Nyongbyon reactor. With those changes, Mexico can support the text.
messages.Norway: Norway supports the draft’s strong condemnation of the 25 May ICBM launch and its clear demand that the DPRK cease destabilizing activities and return to compliance. We ask that the humanitarian provisions expressly guarantee unhindered humanitarian access and adherence to humanitarian principles, especially amid the COVID-19 outbreak. We also want the diplomacy paragraph to call for good-faith efforts aimed at de-escalation and a peaceful resolution.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation cannot accept a text that threatens further significant measures and focuses solely on condemning Pyongyang while ignoring the humanitarian impact and the need for dialogue. We propose removing OP4, balancing the condemnation language, strengthening COVID-19 humanitarian exemptions, and adding a clear call for negotiations without preconditions. The Panel must also act strictly within its mandate and avoid leaks. With these changes, we are ready to engage constructively.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The UAE supports the draft’s clear condemnation of the DPRK’s 25 May ICBM launch and its reaffirmation of existing Security Council measures. We welcome the humanitarian provisions in OP6 and OP8, which help ensure that sanctions do not impede COVID-19-related assistance and medical supplies. We encourage the Council to remain united and to keep the door open to diplomacy and denuclearization negotiations.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom welcomes the US draft and strongly supports its condemnation of the DPRK’s 25 May ICBM launch. We would like OP1 to demand that the DPRK cease preparations for a nuclear test, given the reported activity at Punggye-ri, and OP4 to make clear that additional targeted sanctions will follow further ICBM launches or a nuclear test. We support the humanitarian language in OP6 and OP8 and stress that exemptions must be implemented fully without undermining the sanctions regime.

steps.summary: The revision preserves strong condemnation of the 25 May ICBM launch and CVID demands while removing the automatic threat of further significant measures and adding a no-new-sanctions clause to address P5 red lines. Humanitarian exemptions, dialogue, incident reporting, and sanctions-evasion language are strengthened. The text is expected to secure broad support without a negative vote from any permanent member.

messages.Albania: Albania supports the revised draft as it stands. It delivers a clear and strong condemnation of the DPRK’s ICBM launch, reaffirms the sanctions regime and its full implementation, and includes important humanitarian and human rights language. We urge all Council members to vote in favour so that the Council speaks with one voice.
messages.Brazil: Brazil supports the revised draft and would vote in favour. The text now clearly prioritises dialogue, de-escalation and humanitarian exemptions while stressing that no new sanctions are envisaged. We appreciate the penholder's flexibility in accommodating our concerns.
messages.China: China appreciates the penholder’s partial acceptance, including removal of the new-sanctions threat and addition of dialogue, humanitarian and confidentiality language. We still need OP1 to be balanced: 'expresses concern' and 'calls upon' rather than 'condemns in the strongest terms' and 'demands'. We also ask that OP4 avoid an automatic review trigger and that OP7 explicitly mention addressing each other’s legitimate security concerns; with these changes China can support the text.
messages.France: France welcomes the inclusion of financial and cyber-enabled sanctions evasion and the humanitarian provisions, but the Council cannot respond to the 25 May ICBM launch with condemnation alone. We therefore ask the penholder to restore the targeted sanctions measures we proposed—at minimum the 25 per cent reduction in refined petroleum imports and the tobacco ban—and to strengthen OP4 so that further destabilizing actions will be met with further significant measures. France remains committed to Council unity and will not block consensus if the text is put to the vote.
messages.Gabon: Gabon thanks the penholder for reflecting our key concerns on the review clause, humanitarian exemptions and inclusive dialogue. We support the current text, which rightly condemns the DPRK’s destabilizing missile launches while preserving space for diplomacy and humanitarian action. We encourage all Council members to unite behind this balanced resolution.
messages.Ghana: Ghana supports the current text as a balanced and proportionate response to the DPRK’s 25 May ICBM launch and other ballistic missile activities. We welcome the strengthened provisions on humanitarian exemptions, COVID-19 assistance, dialogue and the good offices of the Secretary-General, which address the concerns we raised in the previous round. Ghana encourages all parties to exercise restraint, avoid escalation and pursue denuclearization through peaceful means.
messages.India: India supports the current text. We note that our earlier concerns on incident reporting by the Panel of Experts and on dialogue by all relevant parties have been accommodated. We welcome the balanced provisions on humanitarian exemptions and the reaffirmation that no new sanctions are envisaged, and we can support the draft.
messages.Ireland: Ireland supports the revised text as it now reflects our key priorities, including a unified Council response to the DPRK’s destabilizing ballistic missile launches, clear humanitarian exemptions and reporting, unimpeded humanitarian access, and express concern at the human rights situation. We welcome the penholder’s constructive engagement and call for the Council to adopt the resolution without delay.
messages.Kenya: Kenya supports the revised text. We welcome the inclusion of clear Committee guidance on humanitarian exemptions, DPRK facilitation of humanitarian access, and balanced language on restraint and de-escalation. We encourage all Council members to support the draft.
messages.Mexico: Mexico supports the current text as revised. We welcome the incorporation of our requests on incident reporting in OP5 and the IAEA/Nyongbyon preambular paragraph. We underline the importance of full implementation of existing measures, effective humanitarian exemptions, and a peaceful diplomatic solution.
messages.Norway: Norway supports the revised draft and welcomes the incorporation of our earlier requests on humanitarian access, humanitarian principles and de-escalation. We ask only that OP7 explicitly reflect the agreed good-faith element by inserting 'in good faith' before 'with a view to de-escalation'. With that technical addition, Norway is ready to vote in favour.
messages.Russian Federation: We support the revised text as a basis and welcome that OP4 now excludes new sanctions and includes review/lifting language. However, the Council cannot adopt a one-sided condemnation while other military activities in the region go unmentioned; PP5 and OP1 must be balanced and call on all parties to exercise restraint. We also ask to delete PP9 on human rights, which is outside the Council's mandate. With these changes we can support the draft.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The United Arab Emirates supports the current text as a balanced and unified response to the DPRK’s destabilizing ballistic missile launches. We welcome the clear reaffirmation of sanctions implementation alongside strong humanitarian provisions, including COVID-19-related exemptions, and the emphasis on dialogue and de-escalation. We encourage the Council to maintain this unity and to keep humanitarian access and diplomatic engagement central to its approach.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The UK welcomes the OP1 language on preparations for a nuclear test and supports the Council’s clear condemnation of the 25 May ICBM launch. However, OP4 as drafted signals that the Council will not respond further to such provocations, which is inconsistent with our shared commitment to hold the DPRK accountable. We ask the penholder to delete the “no new sanctions” sentence and instead state the Council’s determination to take further significant measures, including additional targeted sanctions, in the event of further launches or a nuclear test.

steps.summary: The revised text retains a strong Council condemnation and existing sanctions while adding balanced language on all military activities, good-faith dialogue, and legitimate security concerns. It rejects new sanctions and deletes the human-rights preambular paragraph to secure P5 abstentions, while preserving humanitarian exemptions and Panel of Experts reporting. Expected to pass with at least 10 votes in favour and no negative P5 vote.

reasons.Albania: Albania consistently condemns DPRK missile launches, strongly aligns with the United States and EU/NATO positions, and has no requested changes to this draft. It would speak in favour before the vote to press for Council unity and implementation of existing resolutions.
reasons.Brazil: Brazil has consistently supported Council responses condemning DPRK ballistic missile launches while favoring dialogue and humanitarian safeguards. The draft reaffirms existing measures without new sanctions and includes humanitarian exemptions, so Brazil would vote in favour and has no need to explain before the vote.
reasons.China: China’s core concerns—no new sanctions, humanitarian exemptions, and security-concern language—are largely reflected, and the remaining strong condemnation is balanced by calls for restraint and dialogue, so China would support to avoid obstructing a balanced text.
reasons.France: France prioritizes a unified Council response condemning the DPRK’s ICBM launch and preserving sanctions implementation; although its requested new sanctions measures were rejected, the draft still reaffirms existing sanctions and readiness for further measures, so France votes in favour rather than abstaining or vetoing.
reasons.Gabon: Gabon supports the draft’s firm condemnation of violations, reaffirmation of existing sanctions, and its humanitarian and dialogue provisions, and had no requested changes. It would therefore vote in favour without a pre-vote explanation.
reasons.Ghana: Ghana has supported prior DPRK sanctions resolutions and condemned the recent missile launches, while consistently emphasizing humanitarian exemptions and dialogue. This draft reflects those priorities, so Ghana would vote in favour.
reasons.India: India historically supported Council resolutions on DPRK non-proliferation, and this draft aligns with its position on condemning ICBM launches, supporting denuclearization, and preserving humanitarian exemptions. There is no strong indication India would take the floor specifically before the vote rather than simply voting in favour.
reasons.Ireland: Ireland consistently supports clear Council responses to DPRK ballistic missile violations while insisting that sanctions not harm civilians and that humanitarian exemptions, especially for COVID-19, be ensured; the draft reflects those priorities despite the deletion of the human rights preambular paragraph.
reasons.Kenya: Kenya has consistently condemned DPRK missile launches and supported non-proliferation while emphasising humanitarian access and dialogue; the draft reflects those priorities and contains no new sanctions, so Kenya would vote yes.
reasons.Mexico: Mexico supports the draft’s condemnation of the DPRK’s ICBM launch, reaffirmation of existing sanctions, humanitarian safeguards, and Panel incident reporting, which aligns with its prior concerns. No pre-vote explanation is necessary.
reasons.Norway: Norway consistently supports Council action against DPRK violations, and its requested OP7 language was accepted. It would vote in favour without needing a pre-vote explanation.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia vetoed the US-drafted DPRK resolution on 26 May 2022, opposing one-sided condemnation and further sanctions pressure while advocating dialogue, de-escalation, and humanitarian considerations.
reasons.United Arab Emirates: UAE has consistently supported Security Council action on DPRK non-proliferation, voted in favour of resolution 2627 (2022), and raised no changes to this draft. The text condemns the ICBM launches, reaffirms existing sanctions, and includes humanitarian and diplomatic provisions consistent with UAE priorities.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The UK supports condemning DPRK missile launches and reaffirming sanctions, and the draft partially reflects its request for readiness to take further measures; voting in favour maintains Council unity and pressure on the DPRK.
reasons.United States of America: The United States drafted and strongly supports this resolution as a firm but calibrated response to the DPRK’s 25 May ICBM launch, while reaffirming sanctions, humanitarian carve-outs, and a diplomatic pathway. As a permanent member and the submitting delegation, it would vote yes and explain its support before the vote.

before.Albania: Thank you, Mr. President. Albania will vote in favour of this draft resolution. The Democratic People’s Republic of Korea’s 25 May intercontinental ballistic missile launch and its other recent ballistic missile launches are flagrant violations of Security Council resolutions and dangerous escalations that threaten regional and international peace and security. This Council cannot remain silent while its resolutions are treated as optional. We support this text, which condemns the DPRK’s destabilizing actions, demands complete, verifiable and irreversible denuclearization, reaffirms the obligation of all Member States to implement the sanctions measures fully, and also addresses the humanitarian situation, including COVID-19-related assistance and exemptions. We urge all members to support the resolution and to uphold the unity and credibility of this Council.
before.China: China supports the draft resolution. We welcome the provisions on humanitarian assistance, the emphasis on dialogue and the call to address each other’s legitimate security concerns. The resolution does not impose new sanctions measures, which is important for creating a conducive environment for diplomacy. However, China has reservations about the language in paragraph 1. We believe the Council should remain balanced and avoid escalating tensions. We call on all parties to exercise restraint and resume negotiations. China will vote in favour of the draft resolution.
before.France:
Mr. President,

France thanks the United States for its efforts to ensure that the Council responds to the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea’s launch of an intercontinental ballistic missile on 25 May. That launch is a grave violation of Security Council resolutions and a threat to international peace and security. France condemns it in the strongest terms.

The DPRK must abandon all nuclear weapons and existing nuclear programmes in a complete, verifiable and irreversible manner. It must immediately cease all related activities, including preparations at the Punggye-ri site, and fully comply with its international obligations.

France would have preferred the Council to go further and to strengthen the sanctions regime, in particular by reducing refined petroleum imports and restricting other revenue sources. Those proposals were not retained. We nevertheless welcome the resolution’s reaffirmation of existing sanctions and its readiness to consider further targeted measures in the event of new DPRK provocations. Full and effective implementation by all Member States, including measures to counter financial and cyber-enabled evasion, remains essential.

The humanitarian provisions of this text do not weaken the sanctions regime; they confirm that sanctions are not intended to harm the civilian population, especially during the COVID-19 emergency. France will continue to support humanitarian access consistent with humanitarian principles.

For these reasons, France will vote in favour of this resolution. The Council must remain united and firm in the face of the DPRK’s repeated violations.
before.Ghana: Madam President, Ghana has consistently supported the integrity of the Security Council’s non-proliferation decisions and the goal of a peaceful and denuclearized Korean Peninsula. We remain deeply concerned by the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea’s 25 May intercontinental ballistic missile launch and other recent ballistic missile launches, which violate relevant Council resolutions and increase regional and international tensions. The draft before us responds to these developments while also reaffirming the importance of dialogue and ensuring that sanctions do not have adverse humanitarian consequences, particularly given the serious COVID-19 situation in the country. Ghana therefore will vote in favour of the draft resolution and urges the DPRK to cease all destabilizing actions, return to dialogue and comply fully with its international obligations.
before.Ireland: Thank you, President. Ireland will vote in favour of this resolution. The Democratic People’s Republic of Korea’s launch of an intercontinental ballistic missile on 25 May, following so many other launches, is a serious and flagrant violation of Security Council resolutions and a threat to regional and international peace and security. The Council must speak with one clear voice. We welcome that this text demands that the DPRK abandon all nuclear weapons and existing nuclear programmes in a complete, verifiable and irreversible manner, and that it calls for full implementation of the sanctions measures, including by countering financial and cyber-enabled evasion. We also welcome the text’s emphasis that sanctions are not intended to have adverse humanitarian consequences and its calls for the prompt processing of humanitarian exemptions, especially in light of the grave COVID-19 situation in the DPRK, as well as its support for dialogue and diplomacy. Ireland regrets that the reference to human rights was not retained in the text, but we support this resolution because it is important that the Council responds clearly to these violations and keeps the door open to a peaceful, diplomatic solution. We urge the DPRK to cease all destabilizing activities, refrain from any further launches or nuclear test, and return to dialogue.
before.Kenya: Kenya will vote in favour of this draft resolution. The DPRK’s continued ballistic missile launches, including the intercontinental ballistic missile launch of 25 May, are clear violations of relevant Security Council resolutions and threaten regional and global peace, maritime and aviation safety, and the non-proliferation regime. We support the Council’s condemnation and its call on the DPRK to abandon its nuclear and missile programmes and return to dialogue. At the same time, Kenya stresses that sanctions must not harm the civilian population; we therefore welcome the text’s emphasis on humanitarian exemptions, especially amid the COVID-19 outbreak, and its call for a peaceful diplomatic solution, including the resumption of dialogue and denuclearization negotiations. We urge all parties to exercise restraint and to pursue dialogue in good faith.
before.Russian Federation: Mr. President, the Russian Federation cannot support this draft. Despite the efforts of several delegations, the text remains unbalanced. It places the entire responsibility on the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea while failing to give due weight to the legitimate security concerns on the Korean Peninsula, the positive steps that Pyongyang has taken in recent years, and the need to create incentives for dialogue. The retention of the strongest condemnation and the possibility of further sanctions are inconsistent with the goal of de-escalation. At a time when the DPRK is confronting a serious COVID-19 outbreak, the Security Council should not be used to increase pressure and worsen the humanitarian situation. There is no alternative to a political and diplomatic settlement. For these reasons, the Russian Federation will vote against this draft resolution.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom votes in favour of this resolution. We welcome the Council’s clear condemnation of the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea’s 25 May intercontinental ballistic missile launch and other recent ballistic missile launches, which are violations of Security Council resolutions and increase regional and global tensions. The United Kingdom has consistently called for a firm and united response. While we would have preferred language making clear that further targeted sanctions measures will follow in the event of further destabilizing actions by the DPRK, we support this resolution as a necessary signal of Council unity and resolve. We reaffirm that the DPRK must abandon its nuclear weapons and existing nuclear programmes in a complete, verifiable and irreversible manner, cease all related activities, and comply fully with its international obligations. We call on all Member States to implement fully the sanctions adopted by this Council, including by countering financial and cyber-enabled evasion. The humanitarian exemptions and call for unimpeded humanitarian access are important, particularly in light of the COVID-19 outbreak, and sanctions must not impede the delivery of humanitarian assistance. The United Kingdom remains committed to a diplomatic and peaceful solution and to the complete denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula.
before.United States of America: The United States will vote in favour of this resolution. The DPRK’s 25 May ICBM launch is a clear violation of multiple Security Council resolutions and a serious escalation that demands a unified Council response. This text condemns those launches in the strongest terms, reaffirms the DPRK’s obligation to abandon its nuclear programmes in a complete, verifiable and irreversible manner, and calls on all Member States to implement existing sanctions fully, including against financial and cyber-enabled evasion. At the same time, it makes clear that sanctions are not intended to harm the civilian population, and it calls for the prompt and transparent processing of humanitarian exemptions, including for COVID-19 assistance. The United States remains prepared to engage in serious and sustained diplomacy with the DPRK without preconditions, and we urge the Council to speak with one voice in support of denuclearization and peace on the Korean Peninsula.

after.Albania: Thank you, Mr. President. Albania deeply regrets that the Security Council has been unable to adopt this resolution because of the veto of the Russian Federation. The Democratic People’s Republic of Korea’s launch of an intercontinental ballistic missile on 25 May and its other recent ballistic missile launches are flagrant violations of Security Council resolutions and dangerous escalations that threaten regional and international peace and security. This Council had before it a balanced and necessary text: one that condemned those provocations in the strongest terms, demanded the complete, verifiable and irreversible denuclearization of the DPRK, reaffirmed the obligation to implement existing sanctions fully, and also addressed the humanitarian situation, including COVID-19-related assistance and exemptions. Albania voted in favour because we believe the Council must not remain silent when its resolutions are treated as optional. We regret that a single veto has prevented the Council from speaking with one voice today. That sends the wrong signal to Pyongyang and undermines the credibility of this organ. Albania will continue to stand for the full implementation of Security Council resolutions, for accountability, and for a peaceful, diplomatic and denuclearized Korean Peninsula. We urge the DPRK to cease all destabilizing actions and return to dialogue, and we urge all Council members to uphold the responsibilities they have accepted under the Charter.
after.Brazil:
Mr. President,

Brazil voted in favour of the draft resolution and regrets that the Council was unable to adopt it. The Democratic People’s Republic of Korea’s launch of an intercontinental ballistic missile on 25 May, following other recent launches, is a flagrant violation of relevant Security Council resolutions and contributes to a dangerous pattern of escalation. The Council should not remain silent in the face of such actions.

Brazil supported this text because it condemned the launches clearly, reaffirmed the obligation of the DPRK to abandon its nuclear weapons and existing nuclear programmes in a complete, verifiable and irreversible manner, and called for the full implementation of existing sanctions. At the same time, we welcome that the resolution recognised that sanctions are not intended to have adverse humanitarian consequences, particularly at a time when the DPRK is confronting a serious COVID-19 outbreak, and that it reaffirmed the need for a peaceful and diplomatic solution.

The failure of the Council to adopt this resolution should not weaken the international community’s commitment to the non-proliferation regime or to the goal of a peaceful, denuclearised Korean Peninsula. Brazil calls on the DPRK to cease all destabilising actions and to return to dialogue. We also call on all parties to exercise restraint and to create the conditions for de-escalation and sustained negotiations. The Security Council must continue to address this matter actively, transparently and in a manner that is consistent with its responsibilities under the Charter.
after.Gabon:
Mr. President,

Gabon voted in favour of the draft resolution because the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea’s launch of an intercontinental ballistic missile on 25 May, following other recent ballistic missile launches, constitutes a clear violation of relevant Security Council resolutions and a serious threat to regional and international peace and security. Gabon regrets that the Council was unable to adopt the text despite the support of fourteen members. The unity of the Council and the full implementation of its decisions remain essential if we are to advance the complete, verifiable and irreversible denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula.

Gabon reiterates its commitment to non-proliferation and disarmament, including the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons and the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty, and calls on the DPRK to cease all destabilizing actions and return to dialogue. At the same time, we stress that sanctions should not have adverse humanitarian consequences for the civilian population, particularly in light of the serious COVID-19 situation. We urge all parties to exercise restraint and to pursue a peaceful, diplomatic settlement on the Korean Peninsula.
after.India:
Thank you, Madam President. India voted in favour of the draft resolution. We deplore the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea’s launch of an intercontinental ballistic missile on 25 May and its other recent ballistic missile launches. These launches violate relevant Security Council resolutions, undermine peace and security in the region and beyond, and go against the denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula. They also contravene the DPRK’s own self-declared moratorium. We call upon the DPRK to cease all destabilizing actions, refrain from further missile launches or nuclear tests, and comply fully with its international obligations.

India has consistently supported the complete denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula through peaceful means and dialogue. We call for the full and effective implementation of all relevant Security Council resolutions. In this context, we also recall our request to the Panel of Experts to provide incident reports on missile launches in accordance with its mandate.

The humanitarian situation in the DPRK, including the COVID-19 outbreak, remains a matter of serious concern. Sanctions should not have unintended adverse humanitarian consequences for the civilian population, and humanitarian assistance should be facilitated.

We urge all parties to exercise restraint, avoid actions that increase tensions, and return to diplomacy and dialogue. India will continue to support a peaceful political solution on the Korean Peninsula and the Council’s unity in pursuit of that objective.
after.Ireland: Thank you, President. Ireland voted in favour of this resolution because the DPRK’s 25 May intercontinental ballistic missile launch and its other recent launches are flagrant violations of Security Council resolutions and a serious threat to regional and international peace and security. We deeply regret that this Council has been prevented from adopting a clear and unified response. The overwhelming majority of members supported this text. The DPRK should hear that message clearly: it must cease all destabilizing actions, abandon its nuclear weapons and existing nuclear programmes in a complete, verifiable and irreversible manner, and comply with its international obligations. At the same time, Ireland stresses that sanctions must not have adverse humanitarian consequences. Humanitarian exemptions, including for COVID-19 assistance, must be processed promptly and transparently. Ireland remains committed to diplomacy and to a peaceful resolution of this crisis, but the Council’s credibility depends on its ability to uphold its own decisions. We regret the use of the veto in this context and will continue to support transparency and accountability whenever the veto is used. We urge the DPRK to return to dialogue and all parties to exercise restraint.
after.Mexico: Mexico voted in favour of this draft resolution. We regret that it was not adopted owing to the negative vote of a permanent member. The Democratic People’s Republic of Korea’s launch of an intercontinental ballistic missile on 25 May and its other recent ballistic missile launches are clear violations of relevant Security Council resolutions and constitute a serious threat to regional and international peace and security. The Council had before it a balanced text that condemned those launches, reaffirmed the obligation of the DPRK to abandon its nuclear weapons and existing nuclear programmes in a complete, verifiable and irreversible manner, called for full implementation of existing sanctions, and requested the Panel of Experts to report on ballistic missile launches, including information on the type of missiles, technology and capacities involved. It also contained important provisions on humanitarian exemptions and dialogue. Mexico regrets that the Council could not speak with one voice in the face of actions that undermine the non-proliferation regime. We reiterate our call on the DPRK to cease all destabilizing actions, return to dialogue and comply fully with its international obligations. Mexico will continue to support the Council’s active engagement on this matter and the full and effective implementation of its resolutions, while ensuring that humanitarian considerations, including the serious COVID-19 situation, are duly addressed.
after.Norway:
Thank you, Mr President. Norway voted in favour of this draft resolution. The Democratic People’s Republic of Korea’s launch of an intercontinental ballistic missile on 25 May and its other recent ballistic missile launches are flagrant violations of relevant Security Council resolutions and a serious threat to regional and international peace and security. They contribute to the development of the DPRK’s weapons of mass destruction and ballistic missile programmes and undermine the non-proliferation regime.

Norway deeply regrets that the Council was unable to adopt this resolution owing to the negative vote of a permanent member. At a time when the Council should speak with one clear voice, this veto prevents the Council from responding clearly to these violations. We stress that the DPRK must abandon all nuclear weapons and existing nuclear programmes in a complete, verifiable and irreversible manner and fully comply with its international obligations.

Norway will continue to support the full and effective implementation of existing sanctions, including efforts to counter financial and cyber-enabled evasion, while insisting that sanctions must not have adverse humanitarian consequences for the civilian population, particularly given the serious COVID-19 situation in the DPRK. We urge the DPRK to cease all destabilizing actions, return to dialogue, and engage in serious negotiations aimed at denuclearization and lasting peace on the Korean Peninsula.
after.Russian Federation: Mr. President, the Russian Federation voted against this draft resolution. We did so not because we question the importance of non-proliferation, but because the text remained unbalanced and one-sided. It placed all responsibility on the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea while ignoring the legitimate security concerns on the Korean Peninsula and the positive steps Pyongyang has taken in recent years, including its moratorium on nuclear and intercontinental ballistic missile testing. The retention of the strongest condemnation and the signal that further sanctions could follow are inconsistent with the goal of de-escalation and dialogue. At a time when the DPRK is confronting a serious COVID-19 outbreak, the Security Council should not be used to increase pressure and worsen the humanitarian situation. There is no alternative to a political and diplomatic settlement. Russia remains committed to a peaceful resolution and to creating conditions for negotiations, and we regret that our proposals and the concerns of other delegations were not reflected in the text. We call on all parties to exercise restraint and to return to a balanced and consensus-based approach.
after.United Arab Emirates:
Mr. President,

The United Arab Emirates voted in favour of this draft resolution. We did so because the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea’s recent ballistic missile launches, including the launch of an intercontinental ballistic missile on 25 May, are clear violations of relevant Security Council resolutions and increase tensions on the Korean Peninsula and beyond. We support the Council’s clear message that the DPRK must cease all destabilizing actions, abandon its nuclear weapons and existing nuclear programmes in a complete, verifiable and irreversible manner, and fully comply with its international obligations.

We also welcomed that the text did not impose new sanctions measures, recognized the serious humanitarian situation in the DPRK, including the COVID-19 outbreak, and reaffirmed the need for humanitarian exemptions and for a peaceful, diplomatic solution. The UAE believes that dialogue, restraint and confidence-building are essential. We regret that the Council was unable to adopt this resolution today. The Security Council must remain united and effective in addressing non-proliferation challenges while keeping the humanitarian dimension in view. We urge all parties to return to negotiations and to work toward lasting peace and the denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: Thank you, Mr President. The United Kingdom deeply regrets that the Council has been prevented from adopting this resolution by the veto of the Russian Federation. This was a balanced and proportionate text. It condemned in the strongest terms the DPRK’s 25 May intercontinental ballistic missile launch and other recent ballistic missile launches, which are clear violations of Security Council resolutions. It reaffirmed the requirement that the DPRK abandon its nuclear weapons and existing nuclear programmes in a complete, verifiable and irreversible manner. It called for the full implementation of existing sanctions, including against financial and cyber-enabled evasion. And it made clear that no new sanctions measures were envisaged, while addressing humanitarian concerns, including the COVID-19 situation. There was no justification for blocking a unified Council message in response to such clear and repeated violations. The Russian Federation’s veto does not alter the United Kingdom’s position. We remain committed to a diplomatic solution and to the complete, verifiable and irreversible denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula. We will continue to work with partners to uphold the sanctions regime, to hold the DPRK accountable, and to support the protection of the civilian population. We urge the DPRK to cease all destabilizing actions, return to dialogue, and comply fully with its international obligations. The Council must not remain silent in the face of this growing threat.
after.United States of America: Mr. President, the United States deeply regrets that the Security Council was unable to adopt this resolution today. Fourteen members sent a clear and united message that the DPRK’s 25 May intercontinental ballistic missile launch and its other ballistic missile launches are unacceptable violations of Council resolutions and a serious threat to international peace and security. It is deeply regrettable that one permanent member chose to block that message. A veto cannot erase the DPRK’s violations, and it will not weaken our resolve. The United States will continue to work with allies and partners to implement existing sanctions fully, counter sanctions evasion, including financial and cyber-enabled evasion, and respond to further provocations. We remain open to serious and sustained diplomacy toward the complete denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula, and we remain committed to addressing the humanitarian situation, including COVID-19 assistance, consistent with our sanctions and humanitarian exemptions. We urge the DPRK to cease all destabilizing actions, refrain from any nuclear test, and return to dialogue. This Council must not remain silent in the face of these threats, and the United States will remain actively seized of the matter.
